But then it'll swing the other way, and I'll feel this heavy, empty sadness in my chest and feel completely wiped out, like my body is made of lead.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me more about how long these episodes of feeling 'pumped up' and then 'heavy sadness' last, and do you notice any triggers that seem to set them off?\n\nPatient: These wild swings between feeling pumped up and crashing have been going on for at least the last couple of months, but this heavy, low sadness has been constant for about a month now. It really started with the pressure of a busy wedding season and taking on too many volunteer commitments, but things got much worse when an angry client canceled a major commission, which really set off these heavy, guilty feelings.\n\nDoctor: Can you estimate how many days at a time you experience these elevated moods with increased energy and talkativeness, and do these episodes always end in a crash to the low, sad feelings you described?\n\nPatient: Those high, buzzing energy periods lasted for several weeks at a time when I was rushing to finish all those wedding orders over the last couple of months. It absolutely ended in a major crash, and I've been stuck in this heavy, low spell for about a month now, starting right after that angry client canceled on me.\n\nDoctor: Can you clarify if these episodes of elevated mood and increased energy, followed by crashes into low, sad feelings, have been recurring over the couple of months, or if this is more of a single cycle you've experienced?\n\nPatient: It has definitely been multiple back-and-forth swings over the last couple of months, where my mood and energy would shoot way up and then crash. But while I had those rolling ups and downs before, this current heavy, exhausted low spell has been completely stuck and constant for about the last month since that client issue blew up.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me more about the longest period you've experienced one of these high-energy episodes, and did it last for at least a week, which might help us understand your condition better?\n\nPatient: Yes, those high-energy periods definitely lasted for a week or more at a time during this busy season, where I felt constantly wired and active. Looking back over the last couple of months, there were stretches of two or three weeks straight where I was just buzzing around the shop nonstop.\n\nDoctor: You mentioned feeling guilty, especially after the client canceled the commission; can you describe how intense these guilty feelings are and if they're present even when you're in one of your high-energy phases?\n\nPatient: During my low periods, the guilt is overwhelming; I constantly beat myself up, replay that angry client's email, and feel like I don't deserve anyone's trust. But during my high-energy phases, that guilt completely disappears and I feel incredibly confident, like I'm the best jeweler in north Georgia and can handle anything without help.\n\nDoctor: Do you experience any periods where you have an inflated sense of self-importance or grandiosity during these high-energy phases, beyond just feeling confident in your abilities as a jeweler?\n\nPatient: Yeah, looking back, it definitely crosses the line into something grander than just regular confidence. I catch myself thinking I'm the absolute best jeweler in north Georgia and that I can handle any order without help, even bragging to folks at church about how my business is about to blow up online. I'll say all that even though, deep down, a part of me knows I'm actually drowning in work.\n\nDoctor: Can you think of any instances during these high-energy periods where you engaged in impulsive or reckless behaviors, such as excessive spending or risky business decisions, that might have been influenced by this grandiose thinking?\n\nPatient: Because I felt like I was unstoppable and didn't need any help, I made some really risky decisions by overcommitting to way too many complex custom orders with crazy deadlines. I just kept saying yes to everyone and everything, truly believing I could easily handle it all. It completely backfired on me, leading to missed deadlines, terrible online reviews, and ultimately losing that huge commission.\n\nDoctor: Can you confirm if the longest duration of your high-energy episodes, where you felt grandiose and engaged in impulsive behaviors, lasted for at least two weeks, helping us distinguish between different conditions?\n\nPatient: I'm not entirely sure of the exact duration of just those high-energy phases on their own. All I really know is that the overall swings back and forth between the highs and the lows have been going on for about a couple of months now.\n\nDoctor: Can you try to estimate or recall if there was ever a continuous period of at least two weeks where you maintained this high-energy, grandiose state without dipping into a low-energy phase?\n\nPatient: Yes, absolutely. Before I crashed into this current low month, there was a stretch of about three or four weeks during the height of the wedding season where I felt continuously \"on\" and high-energy every single day. I didn't feel any dip at all during that time—just constant, nonstop confidence and buzzing energy.\n\nDoctor: Can you confirm if the periods of low energy and depressed mood, like the one you're experiencing now, have lasted for more than two weeks at a time?\n\nPatient: Yes, it has definitely been longer than two weeks. This heavy, low mood and lack of energy have been going on continuously for about a month now, ever since things blew up with that angry client and the canceled commission.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any periods of at least two weeks where you felt relatively stable and normal, without either the high-energy grandiosity or the low, depressed mood, over the course of these last couple of months?\n\nPatient: No, I haven't had any stable or normal periods like that over the last couple of months. It has just been a continuous cycle of wild swings, which then transitioned into this heavy, unbroken low spell for the past month since the incident with my client.\n\nDoctor: Can you confirm if you have experienced any depressive episodes that lasted for more than two weeks without any intervening periods of normal mood or hypomanic symptoms, which could help differentiate between our current diagnostic considerations?\n\nPatient: Yes, I can confirm that. This heavy, low spell where I feel sad, guilty, and completely exhausted has been constant for about a month now, ever since the issue with that angry client. There haven't been any high-energy or normal days at all during this past month—it's just been this continuous low.\n\nDoctor: Can you confirm if this current depressive episode, which has lasted for about a month, is the longest you've experienced during these couple of months, or if there have been other episodes of similar or longer duration?\n\nPatient: Yes, this current low spell is definitely the longest and most persistent dark period I've had during these past couple of months. It started right after that major client blow-up about a month ago, and unlike the quicker swings I was having before, this heavy feeling has just stayed completely stuck.\n\nDoctor: Can you confirm if you've had any previous episodes similar to the ones you've experienced over the last couple of months, either before this period or in past years, which might help us understand if this is a recurring pattern or a new development?\n\nPatient: I don't recall ever having mood swings or sleep issues this extreme in the past. As far as I can remember, this past year—especially the last couple of months—is really the first time my energy and mood have fluctuated so intensely and disrupted my life like this.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced more than one episode of either the high-energy, grandiose state or the low, depressed mood over the course of your lifetime, prior to the last couple of months?\n\nPatient: I'm not really sure, but I don't recall having these extreme high or low swings before the last few months. My mood and energy usually felt much more stable and manageable prior to this recent period.\n\nDoctor: Can you confirm if you have had more than one major depressive episode in your lifetime, outside of the episodes described over the last couple of months, to help clarify your diagnosis?\n\nPatient: I'm not really sure, but I don't think I've ever experienced a depressive episode like this before. This past month is the first time I've ever felt this kind of heavy, constant sadness in my life.\n\nDoctor: Can you confirm if you've experienced any other periods of significant mood elevation or depression before the last couple of months that lasted for more than two weeks, which could help us understand your condition better?\n\nPatient: I'm not really sure, but I don't recall having episodes quite like this before this recent stretch. This is the first time things have ever gotten this bad and disrupted my life so noticeably.\n\nDoctor: Can you confirm that the longest duration of your hypomanic episodes, where you felt grandiose and had increased energy, lasted for at least four consecutive days, but less than two weeks?\n\nPatient: I'm not entirely sure of the exact number of days each of those high periods lasts. However, those energetic, buzzing phases definitely seem to go on for several days at a time during these past couple of months.\n\nDoctor: Can you try to recall if any of your past episodes of high energy and grandiosity, before the last couple of months, lasted for at least four consecutive days?"

It absolutely ended in a major crash, and I've been stuck in this heavy, low spell for about a month now, starting right after that angry client canceled on me.\n\nDoctor: Can you clarify if these episodes of elevated mood and increased energy, followed by crashes into low, sad feelings, have been recurring over the couple of months, or if this is more of a single cycle you've experienced?\n\nPatient: It has definitely been multiple back-and-forth swings over the last couple of months, where my mood and energy would shoot way up and then crash. But while I had those rolling ups and downs before, this current heavy, exhausted low spell has been completely stuck and constant for about the last month since that client issue blew up.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me more about the longest period you've experienced one of these high-energy episodes, and did it last for at least a week, which might help us understand your condition better?\n\nPatient: Yes, those high-energy periods definitely lasted for a week or more at a time during this busy season, where I felt constantly wired and active. Looking back over the last couple of months, there were stretches of two or three weeks straight where I was just buzzing around the shop nonstop.\n\nDoctor: You mentioned feeling guilty, especially after the client canceled the commission; can you describe how intense these guilty feelings are and if they're present even when you're in one of your high-energy phases?\n\nPatient: During my low periods, the guilt is overwhelming; I constantly beat myself up, replay that angry client's email, and feel like I don't deserve anyone's trust. But during my high-energy phases, that guilt completely disappears and I feel incredibly confident, like I'm the best jeweler in north Georgia and can handle anything without help.\n\nDoctor: Do you experience any periods where you have an inflated sense of self-importance or grandiosity during these high-energy phases, beyond just feeling confident in your abilities as a jeweler?\n\nPatient: Yeah, looking back, it definitely crosses the line into something grander than just regular confidence. I catch myself thinking I'm the absolute best jeweler in north Georgia and that I can handle any order without help, even bragging to folks at church about how my business is about to blow up online. I'll say all that even though, deep down, a part of me knows I'm actually drowning in work.\n\nDoctor: Can you think of any instances during these high-energy periods where you engaged in impulsive or reckless behaviors, such as excessive spending or risky business decisions, that might have been influenced by this grandiose thinking?\n\nPatient: Because I felt like I was unstoppable and didn't need any help, I made some really risky decisions by overcommitting to way too many complex custom orders with crazy deadlines. I just kept saying yes to everyone and everything, truly believing I could easily handle it all. This heavy, low mood and lack of energy have been going on continuously for about a month now, ever since things blew up with that angry client and the canceled commission.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any periods of at least two weeks where you felt relatively stable and normal, without either the high-energy grandiosity or the low, depressed mood, over the course of these last couple of months?\n\nPatient: No, I haven't had any stable or normal periods like that over the last couple of months.
